SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

10. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.

13. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
